name: test-hygiene
body:
Root of the test-hygiene tree (feature `test-hygiene`). The repo's test suite has no real differentiation between test tiers: tests cross boundaries freely (a "unit" test opens a database or a temp dir) and the suite has become very slow. This tree DEFINES the tier taxonomy durably so the existing suite can be split and future test tasks can be authored against it.

The taxonomy has three tiers — unit, integration, e2e — whose purity rules and shared strict I/O boundary are pinned in `global.constraint.test-tier-boundaries`; the tier names are already the plan task `tier` vocabulary (unit / int / e2e). The tree decomposes into (a) the tier definitions and their strict no-real-I/O boundary, (b) the fast default suite, and (c) e2e as the real-I/O, effectively-isolated, opt-in final gate. Nothing here changes a test's code; it defines the law the split and every future test task are authored against.

No domain or solution tier is authored for this tree: the taxonomy governs how tests are written and gated, not a new code capability, so a drives/realised-by/implemented-by spine would be fabricated. The requirements carry the acceptance criteria; the global constraint carries the law; requirements.note.test-hygiene-motivation records the decisions.
